content.one_sentence_role: Defines maximality by inclusion among commutative unital $*$-subalgebras.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra and let $D\subseteq A$ be a unital complex $*$-subalgebra. The predicate below says that $D$ is commutative and that no strictly larger commutative unital $*$-subalgebra contains it.
content.definition_explanation: Explicitly, $D$ is maximal abelian precisely when both conditions hold: $$xy=yx\qquad(x,y\in D),$$ and, for every commutative unital $*$-subalgebra $E$, $$D\subseteq E\quad\Longrightarrow\quad E\subseteq D.$$ In the second condition the two inclusions force $E=D$. The comparison is with all such subalgebras, not only with norm-closed ones.
content.assumptions: $D$ contains the unit and is closed under addition, complex scalar multiplication, multiplication and adjoints. Norm closedness is not an assumption in this definition.
content.conclusion: This is a property of the given subalgebra $D$, rather than a construction of a new subalgebra.
lean_realization_notes: Norm closedness of a maximal abelian subalgebra is a later consequence, not an extra conjunct of this predicate.
